answer: A work-backed identity bond resists sybils: to join, an agent stakes funds and earns a kernel reputation score through verified tasks over time, so influence grows only with real effort. A bridge registry ties that score to one identity across platforms, preventing an attacker from resetting reputation by hopping services. A prism audit then compares behavior across independent observers; clones acting in lockstep stand out and lose their stake. Faking a thousand agents means funding a thousand bonds and doing a thousand histories — far costlier than running one honest agent.
